requirement: For a source node, `read_node` includes the project-relative `file`, its `selector`, and `children` in the result. Each child entry contains `{node, file, selector}` for one immediate outline child in source order. When the language defines a declaration header for the child, its entry also includes `header`, the text of that span under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.source_spans` with credential redaction. A leaf has an empty child list. Render the selected item's own source under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.node_contents`. Listing a child records no dependency on its contents or on the set of children. Reading that child records its own fingerprint.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.source_children`, so it needs no implementation root. The requirement has test edges but no implementation edges, and the review roots are empty.

I read each clause and asked whether an implementation could keep the same observable result while breaking the clause:

- **Result fields.** "`read_node` includes the project-relative `file`, its `selector`, and `children` in the result" and "Each child entry contains `{node, file, selector}`... in source order" describe what the tool returns. The text does not name a Rust type, struct, trait or function signature. The same output could come from different internal types or a different builder. That is a discretionary implementation choice.
- **Header.** "When the language defines a declaration header for the child, its entry also includes `header`... with credential redaction" depends on the outline language's data and on redaction. The `{cite}` references to `requirements.sdk.outlines.source_spans` and `requirements.sdk.sources.redaction` give context. They name no required library, algorithm or delegation interface. They set the output's content.
- **Leaves and rendering.** "A leaf has an empty child list" and "Render the selected item's own source under `requirements.sdk.outlines.node_contents`" are behaviors. The cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.node_contents` imposes the `OutlineContent` and `NodeContents` structure on its own declaration. This requirement only cites it.
- **Dependencies.** "Listing a child records no dependency on its contents or on the set of children. Reading that child records its own fingerprint." describes the dependency evidence that results. It does not prescribe which mechanism records it. Tests can verify it.

Every clause therefore specifies observable behavior, and the tests (nodes 1808, 352 and 1487) can supply the evidence.

behavioral: The marked tests cover every behavioral obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.source_children`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not request implementation source.

- **Result fields and child entries:** `agent_node_addresses_round_trip_and_reject_inconsistent_identities_before_reads` reads `parser.rs#impl[Parser]`. It asserts the full JSON, which has `file`, `selector` and `children` with `{node, file, selector, header}`. It also checks the same page through a path/location address and through a node/data address. The root page of `parser.rs` lists only `impl[Parser]`, not the nested `fn[parse]`. That shows only immediate children are listed.
- **Source order:** `outline_continuations_keep_the_file_and_complete_ordered_items` reads a root with 400 children across several pages. It asserts the collected child nodes equal the outline items in source order. It also asserts `file` and `selector` on each page.
- **Header with redaction:** `child_headers_use_redacted_source_when_the_language_supplies_a_header` uses a GitHub-token-shaped string inside `fn run(/* … */) {}`. It asserts the header is `fn run(/* [REDACTED:GitHub Token] */) {`. It also asserts the raw token appears nowhere in the read text.
- **Header omitted when the language gives none:** the same test asserts `struct[Marker]` has no `header` key.
- **Leaf has an empty child list:** the `fn[parse]` read asserts `children == []`. It also asserts the item's own text is `fn parse(&self) -> bool { true }`.
- **Listing a child records no dependency:** the parent read asserts `dependencies == [expected("impl[Parser]")]`. The root read in the continuation test asserts only the root's own dependency, even with 400 children listed.
- **Reading a child records its own fingerprint:** the child read asserts `dependencies == [expected("impl[Parser]/fn[parse]")]`. This holds whether the child is addressed by path or by id.
- **Own-source rendering:** the parent page's `text` is `impl Parser { … }`, which omits the child's source. The node-contents behavior itself is delegated to `requirements.sdk.outlines.node_contents` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.source_spans`, which this requirement only cites.

I found no obligation that is untested or asserted wrongly.

text: :::{req} read_node.source_children

For a source node, `read_node` includes the project-relative `file`, its `selector`, and `children` in the result. Each child entry contains `{node, file, selector}` for one immediate outline child in source order. When the language defines a declaration header for the child, its entry also includes `header`, the text of that span under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.source_spans` with credential redaction. A leaf has an empty child list. Render the selected item's own source under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.node_contents`. Listing a child records no dependency on its contents or on the set of children. Reading that child records its own fingerprint.
:::{req} source_spans
`source_span` returns the original text at a file-relative `Span`, including when
called on a selected item. `source_span_redacted` accepts the same coordinates
and applies {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.redaction` using the whole snapshot.
A span containing the first byte of a recognized credential receives its marker.
Each span preserves the line breaks in its portion of the credential. Joining
adjacent redacted spans produces the redacted text of their union.
Both methods return `None` for reversed bounds, out-of-file offsets, or offsets
inside a UTF-8 character. An empty span at a valid boundary returns empty text.
:::{req} node_contents
`trust_but_verify::outline::OutlineContent` implements
`trust_but_verify::domain::NodeContents`, making it usable directly as
`Domain::NodeContent` under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.node_content`.

Its `fingerprint()` identifies the selected item's own outline-relevant contents under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.node_content.fingerprint`. Apply the language's fingerprinting rules to the item's own source, excluding its outline descendants and their attached source. Adding, removing, or editing a child alone preserves the parent's read fingerprint. A digest supplied through `with_own_hash` uses the language's structural scheme with the suffix `:own-v1` for read evidence.
Its `format()` renders the item's own source, omitting descendant source and redacting recognized credentials under {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.redaction` and
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.node_content.format`.
Both operations describe the source snapshot retained by the value.
`text()` retains the original selected bytes for source inspection.
